subsystems.name: EEG sensor array
subsystems.role: detects brainwaves through the forehead and scalp to identify sleep stages.
parts: dry electrodes (conductive silicone or metal pins)

subsystems.name: Signal processing unit
subsystems.role: filters noise and classifies sleep stages in real time.

subsystems.name: Audio stimulation system
subsystems.role: delivers sound to the inner ear without blocking ear canals.

subsystems.name: Mask body and ergonomics
subsystems.role: holds electrodes in stable contact while remaining comfortable for sleep.

subsystems.name: Power and connectivity
subsystems.role: runs the device and syncs data to a phone.

subsystems.name: Companion app
subsystems.role: displays sleep data and lets the user adjust stimulation settings.

buildSteps.title: Design electrode layout
buildSteps.detail: Determine positions on the forehead and scalp that give reliable EEG while lying down, avoiding hair and pressure points.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate dry electrodes
buildSteps.detail: Mould conductive silicone or machine metal pins so they make stable contact without gel and do not irritate skin.

buildSteps.title: Assemble flexible electronics
buildSteps.detail: Integrate amplifiers, microcontroller and Bluetooth onto a flexible printed circuit board that bends with the mask.

buildSteps.title: Integrate bone conduction transducers
buildSteps.detail: Place transducers near the temples or cheekbones so sound travels through bone to the inner ear without covering the ear.

buildSteps.title: Develop sleep staging algorithm
buildSteps.detail: Collect EEG data from many subjects alongside polysomnography labels, then train a classifier to recognise sleep stages in real time.

buildSteps.title: Implement closed-loop stimulation
buildSteps.detail: Define rules for when to play audio (e.g., during a specific sleep stage) and choose sound frequencies and volumes that do not wake the user.

buildSteps.title: Test and validate
buildSteps.detail: Compare sleep quality with and without stimulation using polysomnography and subjective reports, checking for unintended arousals.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture and assemble
buildSteps.detail: Cut and sew fabric, fit electronics and padding, run quality control on electrode contact and audio output, then package.

prerequisites.why: consumer headbands already record brainwaves without gel, though signal quality is lower than with wet electrodes.
algorithms can classify light and deep sleep reasonably well, but detecting REM from a few forehead electrodes is less reliable.
used in headphones and hearing aids; it transmits sound without blocking the ear canal.

prerequisites.tech: Understanding of acoustic stimulation on sleep
prerequisites.why: enhancing slow-wave sleep with timed sounds is better studied than deepening REM, which is the claim here.
microcontrollers and Bluetooth radios can run all night on a small battery.
no widely accepted evidence yet shows that consumer masks can reliably deepen REM sleep.

pathway.milestone: consumer sleep masks that track sleep and play audio, mostly targeting slow-wave sleep
pathway.unlocks: widespread familiarity with wearable sleep technology.

pathway.milestone: improved algorithms that detect REM in real time from a few dry electrodes
pathway.unlocks: closed-loop stimulation aimed specifically at REM periods.

pathway.milestone: clinical trials measuring whether stimulation actually changes sleep architecture and next-day performance
pathway.unlocks: evidence-based sleep enhancement rather than general wellness claims.

pathway.milestone: personalised sleep therapy integrated with other sensors and treatments
pathway.unlocks: prescriptive use for sleep disorders or cognitive support.
